title: FAQ
heading: Questions you might have.
intro: Reaching out to a therapist for the first time can feel uncertain. Here are some answers to the questions I hear most often.

items.question: How do I know if therapy is right for me?
items.answer: We can explore this during a free 15-minute consultation, where you can share what brings you to therapy and ask questions about working together.

items.question: What happens in the free consultation?
items.answer: It is a 15-minute phone conversation to ask questions, briefly share what has brought you here, and get a sense of whether working together feels right. There is no pressure or commitment.

items.question: How do I prepare for my first session?
How long is each session?
items.answer: Sessions are 50 minutes and are generally held weekly or bi-weekly, depending on your needs.

items.question: Do you offer telehealth?
items.answer: Yes. Telehealth is available to clients located in New York, New Jersey, and California.

items.question: Where is your office?
items.answer: My in-person office is located in New York City. The exact address is shared after we schedule your first appointment.

items.question: What if I need to cancel or reschedule?
How do I find out if my insurance covers out-of-network therapy?
What payment methods do you accept?
What therapeutic approaches do you use?
items.answer: My work draws from EMDR, Internal Family Systems, somatic approaches, attachment-based therapy, cognitive-behavioral approaches, mindfulness, narrative therapy, and psychodynamic therapy, depending on your needs.

items.question: Do you work with a specific population?
items.answer: I work with adults navigating trauma, PTSD, anxiety, grief, loss, and life transitions.

items.question: What if we're not a good fit?
items.answer: The free consultation is a chance for both of us to consider whether working together feels right.
